storm.summary_layperson: No thunderstorm risk in the picture for Riverside this evening — mostly sunny with very little instability in the atmosphere and nothing showing up on radar, though the Sound's usual protective cooling effect is fading fast as the afternoon air cools into evening.
storm.local_effect_blurb: There's no storm around to test the Sound's cooling effect tonight, and that buffer is fading anyway — the air-water gap drops from about 8°F now to roughly 2°F by 7 PM, with meaningful protection gone by about 6:15 PM.
storm.detail_html:
Radar out of KOKX shows no storm cells anywhere near Riverside this evening, and today's HRRR run puts CAPE at just 50 J/kg — essentially no instability to build anything on. The latest Area Forecast Discussion from OKX agrees, noting that "instability is minimal" with only some elevated CAPE on forecast soundings, and that any showers/thunderstorms aren't expected until late Saturday night at the earliest. There are no watches, warnings, or advisories in effect, and 0-6km shear is a strong 49.4 kt out of the WSW — but shear without instability has nothing to organize.

Because there's no storm approaching, the Sound's protective marine-layer effect isn't being tested tonight. For the record, that buffer is thin and shrinking regardless: the air-water temperature gap (the difference between the cooling evening air and the steady 75°F Sound water) is about 8°F right now but is projected to fall below the ~5°F threshold by roughly 6:15 PM, bottoming out near 2°F by 7 PM as the air cools faster than the water. So even if something unexpected did try to develop later in the window, there would be little buffer left to lean on.

Bottom line: a calm, quiet evening for the cove and surrounding towns alike, with essentially no thunderstorm risk. The call would change only if a fresh line of convection appears upstream on radar, which nothing in the current data suggests.

wind.tactics_blurb: Moderate gradient wind, no sea breeze in play — starts around 8 kt out of the WNW but this evening's model run shows the gradient itself fading toward light/variable well before the window closes. Pressure is fairly even across the course; start mid-line and don't rig for anything above light-air numbers late.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
This is a gradient-wind evening, not a sea-breeze day. The air-water temperature difference (deltaT) is 7.7°F, above the 5°F thermal-potential gate, but the sea-breeze station ensemble isn't confirming a real onshore signal — only 21% of coastal stations are reading southerly, well short of what a building sea breeze looks like. So the wind tonight is straight synoptic flow, not Sound-driven thermal.

The authoritative airport-anemometer average is 8.9 kt, right at the moderate-gradient band (8-15 kt). Direction is WNW/W (HRRR forecasting 273-301° through the covered hours), though Riverside YC itself is currently reading more NW (321°) than the wider western-LIS ensemble median (273° W, a 48° gap) — a divergence worth flagging; the cove may be running a touch more NW than the open-Sound read suggests, consistent with local channeling.

Favored side: center. W-WNW flow is channeled down the Sound and often has holes near the CT shore while running stronger mid-Sound, so there's no strong lean toward either shore tonight — start mid-line.

The notable thing about tonight isn't the regime label, it's the trend: HRRR's own hourly output shows this gradient collapsing fast, from 7.9 kt at 5 PM down to 3.2 kt by 7 PM — well beyond the normal 1-2 kt nocturnal softening a moderate-gradient day usually sees. HRRR's usable data ends at 7:00 PM this cycle; the 8, 9, and 10 PM rows are extrapolated continuing that same weakening trend, not reverting back up. Expect the breeze to ease toward light/variable numbers by dusk, with real postponement risk if it settles under 3 kt for the back half of the window.

data_caveats: HRRR forecast beyond 7:00 PM (fh05–fh12) unavailable this cycle — 8/9/10 PM wind rows are extrapolated from the observed weakening trend, not model output.
